mcqs.question: Which statement best defines the property of gases that they "fill any available space"?

options.A: Gases spread out to occupy the entire container they are placed in.
options.B: Gases keep the same shape as the container they were originally in.
options.C: Gases remain in a fixed volume regardless of the container size.
options.D: Gases can only fill the bottom part of a container like liquids.

mcqs.answer: Gases spread out to occupy the entire container they are placed in.
mcqs.explanation: Gases have no fixed shape or volume, so their particles move freely and spread out to fill the whole space of any container. Option B is wrong because gases do not keep a shape; Option C is false because gases change volume; Option D describes liquids, not gases.

mcqs.question: Which observation best shows the ability of a gas to flow?

options.A: A balloon staying inflated without moving.
options.B: A perfume scent spreading across a room.
options.D: A rock remaining stationary on a table.

mcqs.answer: A perfume scent spreading across a room.
mcqs.explanation: When perfume is sprayed, its molecules move and spread through the air, demonstrating that gases can flow and mix. The other options do not involve gas movement.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an everyday example that illustrates the compressibility of gases?

options.B: Pressing the piston of a bicycle pump to fill a tire with air.
options.C: A solid iron nail being hammered into wood.

mcqs.answer: Pressing the piston of a bicycle pump to fill a tire with air.
mcqs.explanation: When the piston is pushed, the air inside the pump is forced into a smaller space, showing that gases can be compressed. The other options involve liquids or solids, which are not easily compressible.

mcqs.question: Which of the following substances is a gas at room temperature?
mcqs.explanation: Oxygen exists as a gas under normal atmospheric conditions. Water is a liquid, iron is a solid metal, and sugar is a solid crystalline substance at room temperature.

mcqs.question: Which statement about the shape of a gas is correct?

options.A: Gases have a fixed shape like a solid block.
options.B: Gases take the shape of the container they are placed in.
options.C: Gases keep the shape of the container they were first poured into, even if moved.
options.D: Gases have a shape that depends on temperature only.

mcqs.answer: Gases take the shape of the container they are placed in.
mcqs.explanation: Gas particles move freely and spread out, so a gas always adopts the shape of whatever container holds it. Option A describes solids, C is false because gases change shape with the container, and D confuses shape with other properties.

mcqs.question: Why does a gas not have a fixed volume?

options.A: Because gas particles are tightly packed and cannot move.
options.B: Because gas particles are far apart and can be moved closer together.
options.C: Because gas particles are glued together forming a rigid structure.
options.D: Because gas particles are attracted strongly to the walls of the container.

mcqs.answer: Because gas particles are far apart and can be moved closer together.
mcqs.explanation: Gas particles are spaced widely, allowing them to be compressed into a smaller volume. Options A and C describe solids, while D is incorrect because gases are not strongly attracted to container walls.

mcqs.question: How does the ability of a gas to fill available space differ from that of a liquid?

options.A: Both gas and liquid fill the shape of their container, but only gas also fills the entire volume of the container.
options.B: Both gas and liquid have fixed volumes, so neither fills the entire container.
options.C: Only liquids fill the shape of the container, while gases keep their original shape.
options.D: Gases fill the shape of the container, whereas liquids expand to fill the entire container.

mcqs.answer: Both gas and liquid fill the shape of their container, but only gas also fills the entire volume of the container.
mcqs.explanation: Liquids take the shape of the container but have a fixed volume, so they do not occupy the whole container if it is larger than the liquid amount. Gases, however, expand to occupy all available space, both shape and volume. Options B, C, and D misstate the properties of liquids and gases.

mcqs.question: In a sealed balloon, which property of the gas inside allows the balloon to change shape when it is squeezed?

options.A: The gas particles are rigid and cannot move past each other.
options.B: The gas particles have the ability to flow past each other.
options.C: The gas has a fixed volume that resists any shape change.
options.D: The gas particles are attracted strongly to each other, keeping the shape constant.

mcqs.answer: The gas particles have the ability to flow past each other.
mcqs.explanation: Gases consist of particles that move freely and can slide past one another, which lets the balloon deform under pressure and then return to its original shape when released. Options A and D incorrectly describe solid-like behavior, and C contradicts the compressible nature of gases.
